newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTORCYCLING-OKADA SNATCHES POLE AS HONDA MEN REIGN IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-OKADA SNATCHES POLE AS HONDA MEN REIGN IN SPAIN.

text.p: Tadayuki Okada squeezed ahead of teammates Michael Doohan and Alex Criville on Saturday to snatch a surprise pole position for the Spanish 500 cc motorcycle Grand Prix.

Okada improved his time from Friday's wind-affected first qualifying session by over a second and a half to set a new lap record on the Jerez track. A fourth Honda man, Nobuatsu Aoki, will complete the front row of the grid for Sunday's race.
Three-times world champion Doohan quickly took advantage of the sunny conditions to wrest provisional pole from Alberto Puig.

Although Puig was relegated to the second row of the grid after going quickest on Friday, the home fans were able to cheer the efforts of Criville, who went within two-tenths of a second of his arch-rival Doohan.
But with just four minutes of qualifying remaining, Okada jumped up four places to upset what seemed to be the latest chapter in the Doohan-Criville domination of the world championship.
Doohan reappeared on the track, but was unable to dislodge Okada, and will have to start in second in his bid to equal Mike Hailwood's record of 37 wins in 500cc Grand Prix.
